data.gender_notes: Hal is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Hal means 'rock' or 'hale.' It is also derived from the name Hades, the Greek god of the underworld. In Christianity, the name Hal may symbolize strength, resilience, and fortitude. The name Hal carries the meaning “Rock, Hale” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hal usually hope their child will grow to embody rock, hale and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of strength and resilience in the face of challenges.
data.etymology: Hal belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rock, Hale.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hal total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Hal was used as a given name in the Middle Ages, and it gained popularity during the Crusades when the name was given to valiant warriors. The name Hal represents the idea of a strong and steadfast individual, symbolizing the warrior archetype.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, the name Hal symbolizes spiritual strength and resilience. It is inspired by the Biblical character named Gideon, who led the Israelites to victory against the Midianites despite his initial doubts and fears. The name Hal, therefore, reminds us to trust in God's strength and provision during times of challenge and adversity.
